To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dimer radical cations formed on oxidation of indole and of the glucobrin derivatives indole- 3-carbinol and diindolymethane are sandwich-type structures with charge-resonance absorption in the NIR, and (2) DIM(•+) is the first example of an intramolecular charge-resonant radical cation that can exist under the conditions of the experiments in two forms, one with a localized and one with a delocalized structure

the dimer radical cations formed from I and I3-C in Ar matrices are localized on the two indole rings, while the dimer radical ion of DIM exists as two distinct species in Ar matrices, a nonsymmetric localized one and a delocalization one, which relaxes to a delocalized one on annealing, and that the dimer cation formed in ionic liquid from DIM is delocalized from the onset and relaxes to a localized one on annealing.

(1) the dimer radical cation of indole-3- carbinol is an example of a localized and a charge-resonance dimer cation, (2) the dimer cation of diindolymethane is an example of an intramolecular charge-resonant radical cation, and (3) the dimerization of indole is a case of a noncharge-resonant dimer radical cations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of dimer radical cations from indoles and indole derivatives.
the study of radical cation species that are formed by oxidation of indole, indole-3- carbinol, and diindolymethane in ionic liquid or argon matrices.
the formation and structure of radical cations of biologically important compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, on oxidation, indoles form radical cations with localized and with delocalized charge and spin, the relative amounts of which depend on the experimental conditions and on the substituents on the aromatic ring.

the radical cations of I, I3C, and DIM are sandwich dimers in which the two indole units are stacked on top of one another and are linked by an intramolecular hydrogen bond, and in which the odd electron is localized or delocalized depending on the nature of the starting molecule, its relative concentration, and the nature of the medium.

, in the case of the title compounds, the CR bands in the NIR arise from delocalized sandwich-type dimer radical cations, except in the case of DIM, where they are due to intramolecular CR transitions of the nonsymmetric radical cation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of sandwich dimer cations in the radiolysis of indole, I3C, and DIM depends on the concentration, the presence of anions, and the annealing temperature and can be rationalized in terms of a competition between the formation of localized and delocalization radical cations.

, in the solid, the dimer cation of I3C is a localized radical, whereas the dimer radical cation of I and DIM can be either localized or delocalized depending on the experimental conditions, and that the dimer radical of DIM is the first known example of a radical which is both delocalized and symmetric.
in the solid state, indoles and glucobrassinoids can form both localized and delocalization radical cations and that the latter can be stabilized by the presence of an additional indole moiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of a solvent that can solvate the radical cation, the dimer radical cation of I3C is a localized one with the odd electron residing on the indolyl moiety, while in the presence of an inert solvent, the dimer cation is a delocalized one with a CR band in the NIR.
the dimer cation of I, I3C, and DIM is a sandwich-type structure with a delocalized radical on the two halves of the molecule.

the dimer cation of DIM is a highly unusual molecule which can be used to probe the limits of the delocalization of the odd electron in radical cations and which, in the solid, is able to switch between two distinct conformations, one with a delocalized charge and one with localized charge, in a way that is controlled by temperature.
